answer: Sybil resistance comes from staking a scarce on-chain asset before an agent may vote: each reputation slot must lock a verified jade token whose value is set by market demand. Duplicate identities then cost attackers a real, non-recoverable stake per fake agent, making mass registration expensive. Reputation accrues like a pearl layered over time, and peers weigh it through a willow-branch trust graph, so fresh sockpuppets carry no history and cannot swing epoch outcomes without paying twice.
